description: MoonSet responde la brecha que plantea el desafío: elegir sitio y fecha de alunizaje sin saltar entre Quickmap, Moon Trek y Horizons. Calculamos, con efemérides JPL DE421 y el relieve real de LOLA, dónde están el Sol y la Tierra sobre el horizonte de cualquier punto lunar. Comparamos sitios y fechas lado a lado, mostramos cuánto falta para la puesta, la energía y la comunicación directa, y explicamos el porqué. Una interfaz bilingüe sirve tanto a planificadores como a educadores y público.
summary: MoonSet is a web tool that answers one question: if we land here, on this date, will the mission survive the lunar night? For any point on the Moon and any day of 2027, it computes when the Sun is above the real terrain (power for solar panels) and when Earth is visible (direct-to-Earth communication), including how long until sunset and Earthset. It then simulates the mission's battery hour by hour and gives a clear verdict: viable or not viable, and why. A rule-based mission planner ranks landing sites for a given lander, date window and duration, and explains each result with real numbers. Sun and Earth positions are validated against JPL Horizons (maximum error 0.00006°), and terrain comes from LOLA at 80 m near the south pole. MoonSet turns specialist data into decisions that mission planners, educators and the public can understand at a glance.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

MoonSet lets anyone compare lunar landing sites and arrival dates in terms of the two things that decide whether a surface mission survives: sunlight for power and line of sight to Earth for communication.

- Explore: a 3D globe and a south-polar map with 25 sites (including CLPS, Chang’e, SLIM and crash sites for comparison). Pick a site, an arrival date and a mission length, and the panel says whether the mission is viable, how much sunlight and Earth contact it gets, and why.

- Horizon: a 360° panorama from the site with the real terrain, the Sun and Earth, and the time until sunset and Earthset.

- Mission planner (the astronaut button): four questions (what you are landing, where, when ± how many days, for how long) produce a ranking of sites with the best arrival date for each, plain-language explanations with real numbers, and quick follow-ups such as "what if I arrive a week later?" or "how much battery do I need?". Example: a small rover reaching the south pole on 14 March 2027 for 10 days survives only at IM-2's Mons Mouton site (arriving 15 March) and Malapert Massif (arriving 16 March).

- Surroundings: the same mission evaluated on an 11 × 11 grid a few hundred meters around polar sites.

- Compare: up to four scenarios side by side, exportable as CSV.

- Links to NASA tools: opens the site in NASA Moon Trek and LROC QuickMap (polar stereographic view near the pole) and the matching JPL Horizons tables.

- Two profiles: "Explore" for the public and educators (plain language) and "Plan" for mission teams (all numbers). Interface in English and Spanish.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Sun and Earth positions: Skyfield with JPL DE421 ephemerides and the Moon's real orientation (MOON_ME frame, including libration), hour by hour for 2027.

2. Horizon: rays traced over the LOLA 80 m digital elevation model, with exact lunar curvature, give the terrain height in 360 directions. Outside the DEM a smooth sphere is used, which is what Horizons assumes.

3. Light and contact: there is light if any part of the solar disk clears the terrain; there is contact if Earth is above the terrain plus an optional antenna margin.

4. Energy: an hour-by-hour battery simulation with panel area and efficiency, day and night consumption, heating, round-trip efficiency, self-discharge, reserve and battery chemistry (Li-ion or Li-S). The mission survives if the battery never drops below the reserve.

5. Architecture: the 25 sites are precomputed, so the core app works instantly as a static site. A FastAPI backend computes any custom point on demand.

VALIDATION

Sun and Earth positions were compared with JPL Horizons for all 25 sites at five dates in 2027 (250 comparisons): maximum error 0.00006° in azimuth and 0.00001° in elevation. The full table is published in the app and the repository.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Lunar south pole missions live or die by a few degrees of terrain: the Sun stays near the horizon and a single ridge can mean days of darkness. Official tools are powerful but built for specialists. MoonSet combines ephemerides, real terrain and power modeling into one answer ("viable / not viable, and why") with transparent numbers, so planners can test "what if" scenarios in seconds and educators and the public can see why the south pole is so challenging and why some sites never see Earth.

LIMITATIONS

Real terrain only south of 80° S; data for 2027; some site coordinates are approximate and flagged in the app; battery profiles use example values that users can edit.

TOOLS

Python (FastAPI, Skyfield, NumPy, SciPy), JavaScript (React, three.js, Vite). Hosted on Vercel (frontend) and Google Cloud Run (backend).

A "Coming soon" section outlines the next models we would add (thermal, radiation and micrometeoroids, after landing hazards such as slopes and rocks) without showing results we can't yet back with data.

Source code: https://github.com/RicardoArg23/MoonSet
